points.description: States that more than one routing-table entry (prefix) can match a destination IP address.
States that longest-prefix matching chooses the longest matching prefix because it is the most specific route.
States that longest-prefix matching allows route aggregation/summarization while still permitting more specific exception routes.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all three ideas: multiple matching entries, choosing the longest/most specific prefix, and the benefit of allowing aggregation with exceptions. Each point is all-or-nothing, so an answer missing one idea earns only the marks for the ideas it contains. No marks are given for vague statements that do not mention matching entries, specificity, or aggregation.
